blocks.title: What YMTC is
blocks.text: Yangtze Memory Technologies, Wuhan: China's 3D NAND maker, state-backed (Big Fund, Hubei investors). Its Xtacking design builds the CMOS logic and the NAND array on separate wafers and bonds them. On the US Entity List since Dec 2022. Not listed: parent CCSH filed for a Shanghai STAR Market IPO in Aug 2026, which was reported on hold in Nov 2026. Financials (2023 to Q1 2026) are CCSH consolidated figures from the Aug 2026 STAR IPO prospectus, read from press coverage of it (Caixin, Global Times/SSE, StorageNewsletter, Admirals), not from the prospectus itself. YMTC Co. is over 90% of CCSH revenue.

blocks.title: Why 130k, 160k and 200k all appear
blocks.text: No figure comes from YMTC. ~130k wafer starts/month (Notebookcheck, eefocus via TrendForce) and 160k at end-2024 (analyst reports via Reuters) describe the same two Wuhan fabs at about the same time, so they are a genuine conflict. Reuters' sources put it at ~200k in Apr 2026 while Caixin said ~160k in Aug 2026. Wafer starts (what is running) and installed capacity (what could run) are often mixed. The Korea Herald annual wafer counts work out to ~108k/month in 2024 and ~148k in 2025, nearer the low end.

blocks.title: Gates vs active layers
blocks.text: Layer counts are not one measure. TechInsights counted 294 gates in the Xtacking 4.0 die (150 on the lower deck, 144 on the upper): every gate line in the stack, including dummy and select gates. Active word-line layers that store data are fewer, which is why the same generation is reported as 267 (IPO filing coverage, 'in mass production') and 270 (TrendForce). 232 is the 2022 Xtacking 3.0 part. Korea Herald reports 300+ layers planned for 2026; peers' figures (SK hynix 321, Samsung 286) are also active-layer counts.
